editorial:
Ever feel like you are just stuck in a loop? You will definitely relate to the main character here. She is a suburban mom who has spent her whole life taking care of everyone else, but now she feels totally empty inside. Between the boring house chores and her adult kids who just cannot get their lives together, she is reaching a breaking point. The movie captures that feeling of being trapped in a perfect little neighborhood where everything looks great on the outside, but everyone is actually miserable on the inside. It is a slow-burn story that focuses on the small, annoying moments of family life that eventually lead to a big emotional blowout.

The acting is really solid and makes you feel the frustration of the characters. While some parts of the movie move a bit slow, the honest conversations make it feel real. If you enjoy character studies about family drama, you will love this.
endingExplained: In the end, the mother finally stops trying to fix her children's mistakes. She has a huge argument with her kids where she tells them she is done being their safety net. Instead of staying trapped in her routine, she decides to travel and focus on her own happiness for once. The movie wraps up with her leaving the house behind, showing that letting go of her family's stress was the only way to save herself.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramas and stories about finding yourself.
